correctness.rationale: Normalized positive Shepard weights reproduce constants, reducing arbitrary real triple variation to two unit-step responses. The nonlocal weight on the opposite cell has a unique critical point from an explicitly monotone denominator derivative, with exact value determined by the mesh ratio and exponent; reflection covers the other step. Strict monotonicity in the ratio proves equispaced optimality. Exact asymptotic estimates give the logistic coupled power–mesh boundary layer, including zero and infinite endpoints. The chosen step response attains the bound for all positive parameters. The standard-library checker independently searched extremal responses for 220 random parameter triples and checked supplementary limits; no unproved infinite statement depends on numerical tests.

value.rationale: This computes a natural sharp BV stability invariant across the entire three-site positive Shepard family, not an arbitrary slice: it establishes extremal inputs, the unique optimal mesh, the collapse ceiling of two, and the logistic joint scaling threshold. For irregularly spaced sampling it exposes why positivity/range preservation cannot prevent oscillatory total-variation amplification, even with high inverse-distance powers. These precise stability properties can guide weighting or mesh design; no larger-scale or higher-dimensional conclusion is claimed.
